function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or directive that gives someone the power or right to act on behalf of another party. It can take many forms depending on the context:

| Context | Typical meaning |
|---------|-----------------|
| **Legal / Corporate** | A written or verbal instruction from a principal (e.g., a company’s board) to an agent (e.g., a director or officer) to perform specific actions. |
| **Finance / Banking** | An agreement that authorizes a bank or payment service provider to execute transactions—such as standing orders, direct debits, or electronic funds transfers—on behalf of a customer. |
| **Government / Politics** | A formal statement of policy or direction issued by a governing body or leader, often used to guide the actions of officials or agencies. |
| **Business Partnerships** | A contract that outlines the responsibilities, rights, and obligations of each partner, effectively mandating how they must conduct business together. |

In short, a mandate is a binding instruction that empowers one party to act within defined limits for the benefit or under the authority of another.
